purpose: Agent-facing retrieval layer for southern Magallanes travel, protected areas and territorial connectivity.

chunks.title: Ruta de los Parques overview
chunks.summary: Ruta de los Parques sources describe a 2,800 km conservation and nature-travel corridor linking 17 national parks from Puerto Montt to Cabo de Hornos, integrating the Carretera Austral, Patagonian channels and the Ruta del Fin del Mundo.

chunks.title: National parks in the Magallanes section
chunks.summary: The Ruta de los Parques road map explicitly lists seven national parks in the Magallanes section: Bernardo O'Higgins, Kawésqar, Torres del Paine, Pali Aike, Alberto de Agostini, Yendegaia and Cabo de Hornos.

chunks.title: Yendegaia territorial and conservation context
chunks.summary: Yendegaia is a national park in the far south of Isla Grande de Tierra del Fuego, associated with the Beagle Channel and Cordillera Darwin. Current CONAF information places it in the communes of Timaukel and Cabo de Hornos and describes a mountainous landscape of ice fields, glaciers, fjords and channels.

chunks.title: Current Yendegaia access and visitor-service status
chunks.summary: As of 23 August 2026, CONAF describes maritime access from Puerto Williams/Puerto Navarino toward Bahía Yendegaia and a terrestrial approach via Ruta Y-85 to Lago Fagnano plus the Vicuña–Yendegaia penetration road. CONAF simultaneously states that the park has no visitor attention and no public-use infrastructure.
chunks.prohibited_inference: Do not promise a staffed entrance, public-use facilities, scheduled boat, or completed through-road connection to Puerto Williams.

chunks.title: Vicuña–Yendegaia road remains under construction
chunks.summary: Current 2026 Ejército/CMT and MOP evidence shows the Vicuña–Yendegaia corridor remains under construction. Etapa XI works were active in 2026, including installation of a modular bridge in the Cordillera Darwin front. The corridor must not be represented as a completed continuous public road to Puerto Williams.
chunks.prohibited_inference: Do not state that travelers can currently drive continuously from mainland Chile to Puerto Williams through this project.

chunks.title: TABSA Punta Arenas–Puerto Williams maritime connection
chunks.summary: TABSA currently publishes Punta Arenas–Puerto Williams as a maritime service and describes the crossing as approximately 32 hours. Departure dates, fares, vessel assignment and availability remain booking-sensitive and must be rechecked at answer time.
chunks.prohibited_inference: Do not treat the 2022 map's 31-hour duration as current; current first-party TABSA page says approximately 32 hours.

chunks.title: TABSA service scope includes Caleta 2 de Mayo
chunks.summary: TABSA's current Puerto Williams operations listing includes Punta Arenas, Puerto Williams, Puerto Toro and Caleta 2 de Mayo within its route/service scope. This confirms operator scope, not a guaranteed fixed-frequency itinerary to Caleta 2 de Mayo.
chunks.prohibited_inference: Check the live itinerary before telling a traveler that a Caleta 2 de Mayo sailing is available on a specific date.

chunks.title: Current Cabo de Hornos visitor-access model
chunks.summary: Current CONAF information states that Parque Nacional Cabo de Hornos is open daily 09:00–18:00 with advance ticket purchase through Pases Parques. Access is maritime, commonly after reaching Puerto Williams by air or from Punta Arenas via prearranged navigation circuits. Isla Hornos has a small landing pier and footpath but no lodging, food, basic services or local emergency services.
chunks.prohibited_inference: Do not imply independent walk-in access or guaranteed landing; maritime conditions and operator arrangements still govern practical access.

chunks.title: Current Alberto de Agostini visitor-access model
chunks.summary: Current CONAF information states that Parque Nacional Alberto de Agostini is open daily 09:00–18:00 with advance ticket purchase through Pases Parques. Access is mainly maritime, including private programmed navigation, and the park has no administrative or public-use facilities.
chunks.prohibited_inference: Do not describe the park as having visitor centers, lodging, campsites or staffed public infrastructure unless newer official evidence says so.

chunks.title: Current Primera Angostura crossing
chunks.summary: TABSA identifies Primera Angostura as the ferry crossing between Punta Delgada on the mainland and Bahía Azul on Tierra del Fuego, separated by about 5 km. Operational status is dynamic and should be checked through TABSA immediately before travel.

chunks.title: Puerto Williams–Puerto Toro subsidized maritime service
chunks.summary: In August 2026 the Delegación Presidencial Provincial de Antártica Chilena publishes sailings between Puerto Williams and Puerto Toro under a subsidized isolated-zone maritime service. It is explicitly not a tourism product: Puerto Toro residents have priority for seats and cargo, and dates may change because of weather or community needs.
chunks.prohibited_inference: Do not market or recommend this as a normal sightseeing ferry; availability for visitors is conditional and secondary to resident needs.

chunks.title: Puerto Toro transbordador terminal authorization
chunks.summary: DIRECTEMAR records a May 2025 local resolution enabling operation of the Puerto Toro transbordador terminal on Isla Navarino. This is infrastructure/regulatory evidence and does not by itself establish a current passenger timetable.
chunks.prohibited_inference: Do not derive service frequency or tourism availability from terminal authorization alone.

chunks.title: Puerto Williams and Punta Arenas as southern park gateways
chunks.summary: The 2022 Ruta de los Parques brochure identifies Puerto Williams and Punta Arenas as gateway cities for southern protected-area access, including Alberto de Agostini and the Cabo de Hornos environment. This is route-context evidence, not proof that every current transport service or park access is available from both cities.
chunks.prohibited_inference: Do not infer current ferry, cruise, flight or landing availability from gateway wording alone.

chunks.title: Ruta de los Parques responsible travel principles
chunks.summary: The route passport promotes low-impact travel: protect ecosystems, support local communities, respect traditions, reduce waste, do not feed wildlife, observe fauna from a distance, stay on marked trails, comply with fire bans and follow park-ranger instructions.
